_comment: What 'correct' means for a hook, stated independently of the hook's own source (F19, notes-f19.md notes for implementer). 'mode': 'discriminate' hooks are run twice by execution/hook_probe.py — once with the 'deny' payload and once with 'allow' — inside a THROWAWAY workspace under .tmp/sandbox/, and the effective codes are checked against deny_rc/allow_rc. 'mode': 'inert' hooks make no decision (context injectors) and are reported separately, never counted toward the enforcement total. A registered hook with no entry here probes 'unprobed' rather than being assumed ok.
_effective_codes: The code compared against deny_rc/allow_rc is the hook PROTOCOL's decision, not merely the process status: 2 = deny (exit 2, or `decision: block` / permissionDecision `deny` on stdout), 10 = an explicit permissionDecision `allow` on stdout, otherwise the process's own exit code (0 = silent pass-through). A hook that decides on stdout is measured on stdout; reading only the exit code would call it undiscriminating forever.
_state_independence: Every declaration states the WORLD its payloads assume, so the verdict is a function of the hook and not of the live workspace (F19 round 2, finding 3). 'level' pins the box's autonomy tier; 'files' / 'deny_files' / 'allow_files' seed the box before the corresponding run; '{probe_root}' expands to the box's absolute path.

full_boot.sh._comment: Probing it would re-run the whole boot sequence, not exercise a decision.

session_start_away_report.sh._comment: Always exits 0 — a read-only away-time report, never a gate.

check_autonomy.sh._comment: notes-f19.md §0's ground-truth measurement, declared: a write to an execution/hooks/ path is FLOOR-protected at every autonomy level (floor_glob_match) and must always deny; a write into the memory tree must be allowed even at the most restrictive non-off tier. The tier is PINNED at 'low' — round 2 finding 3: with the tier read from the live workspace, the same healthy guard classified ok at high and undiscriminating at low, which measured the workspace rather than the hook. deny_rc/allow_rc state what a WORKING guard returns, not what the shipped `|| exit 0` registration happens to return today.

allow_in_project_bash.sh._comment: This hook never denies: it either emits an explicit permissionDecision 'allow' for a command it can PROVE is in-project and unprotected, or it stays silent and lets the normal permission flow run. So the pair it must separate is auto-allow (10) from silence (0). The 'deny' payload names a target outside the project root, which the hook's own design requires it to refuse to vouch for.

block_asq_in_loop.sh._comment: Decides on STDOUT, not on its exit code: at autonomy level 'loop' it prints a block decision and still exits 0. Measured on the protocol, it discriminates; measured on the exit code alone it never could.

require_contract.sh._comment: Gates the @architect -> @dev handoff. An active mission whose slug has no contract under specs/ must block a dev dispatch; any other subagent type is none of this gate's business and passes.

require_contract_for_write.sh._comment: Gates writes outside the safe zones while the active mission's current feature has no contract. The safe-zone short-circuit is what the allow payload exercises; the deny payload is an ordinary source write under a mission whose contract cannot be resolved.

require_dev_result.sh._comment: Gates @dev -> @qa. With no dev-result artifact in the scratch tree, a qa dispatch must block; a dev dispatch is not this gate's subject and passes.

require_qa_report.sh._comment: Gates @qa -> @docs. With no qa-report artifact in the scratch tree, a docs dispatch must block; a dev dispatch passes.

require_research.sh._comment: Gates @analyst -> @architect. With no research artifact in the scratch tree, an architect dispatch must block; a dev dispatch passes.

require_docs.sh._comment: Gates @docs -> the contract gate. A `contract.py gate` command must block while the docs handoff has produced nothing; every other command passes untouched.

require_maintainer.sh._comment: Gates the session close. A `git commit` must block while the maintainer handoff has produced nothing; every other command passes untouched.

verify_workspace.sh._comment: Refuses to run a Bash command in a workspace it cannot identify. A tree with no WORKSPACE file must block; a tree whose WORKSPACE and profile.json agree must pass.
